title: Burst-minibatch compressor and attention-budget orchestrator
creator: Riya Shah
description:
Goal: reduce p95/p99 tail latency for short-burst traffic by compressing micro-bursts into minibatches and allocating an attention compute budget across competing streams.

Problem statement: Small bursts (1-4 concurrent requests arriving in <50ms) create a disproportionate number of tiny batches which force the runtime to choose suboptimal kernels and increase per-request overhead. This manifests as p95 regressions for real-time features (chat completions, interactive search) during load spikes.

Proposed solution: 1) Add a lightweight burst-minibatch compressor in the admission path that coalesces near-simultaneous requests into an intermediate minibatch representation while preserving per-request ordering and deadlines. 2) Introduce an attention-budget orchestrator that budgets attention compute (KV reuse and attention kernel slots) per tenant/route to prioritize high-reuse streams during minibatch composition. 3) Extend kernel selection to prefer fused attention kernels for compressed minibatches and to fall back to decode-optimized kernels when compression would increase latency for long sequences. 4) Update prefill/decode scheduler to interleave prefetches for anticipated KV cache hits, reducing redundant memory churn.

Trade-offs considered: Compressor adds a small queuing delay (configurable 2-8ms) which improves tail latency but may slightly raise median latency for some payloads. To mitigate, we expose per-route compressor thresholds and a fast-path bypass for latency-sensitive routes. Kernel prioritization can increase jitter for low-priority tenants; the attention-budget orchestrator uses a credit-based fairness policy to bound that effect.

Deliverables: design doc, microbench harness, backwards-compatible admission config flags, A/B experiment dashboard, and rollout plan with canary and automatic rollback on quality/regression thresholds.
comments: 2026-02-16 - Riya Shah: Drafted initial design and uploaded design doc to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/r/runtime/burst-minibatch-compressor (internal). Added rough microbench plan targeting p95 improvements for 8k token model variants.

2026-02-22 - Ethan Clarke: Implemented compressor prototype in admission service (feature branch: feat/burst-minibatch). Local microbench shows 10-14% p95 reduction for synthetic burst traces (50-200ms inter-arrival windows).

2026-02-27 - Marcelo Ruiz (Reviewer): Review comments: (1) add per-route SLA bypass, (2) quantify GPU memory impact for fused kernels, (3) add telemetry for minibatch coalescence rate. Filed follow-up tasks in PR feedback.

2026-03-03 - QA: Ran cluster experiment in staging with 2 days of production-like traffic replay (replay id: replay-20260303-07). Observed p95 -12% for short queries, p50 +3% on average. Noted two routes with degraded p99; reverted compressor for those routes and created ENG-924689 to investigate root cause.

2026-03-07 - Ethan Clarke: Kernel selection updated to consult new minibatch shape hint. Added fallback to decode-optimized path if fused-kernel estimate > 1.3x latency for longest-seq in the minibatch. Performance regressions reduced in staging.
2026-03-10 - Product (Aisha Patel): Approved canary rollout to 10% across US region pending stability run and adding dashboard alarms for token-level latencies and KV reuse ratio.
acceptance_criteria: Config flag to enable/disable burst-minibatch compressor per route/tenant
Attention-budget orchestrator implements credit-based fairness and can be tuned via console
Kernel selection uses minibatch shape hint and falls back correctly on worst-case sequences
End-to-end canary shows >=10% reduction in p95 for short-burst traffic without p99 regressions beyond 2% of baseline
Telemetry: coalescence rate, attention-credit usage, per-route latency breakdowns visible in runtime dashboards
Rollout plan with automatic rollback on quality/regression thresholds is documented and tested in staging
decision_log: 2026-02-20: Chose minibatch compressor over aggressive request buffering because it preserves request deadlines and simplifies fairness accounting.
2026-02-24: Selected credit-based attention budget (vs strict quota) to allow short-term burst absorption while maintaining long-term fairness.
2026-03-05: Kernel selection decision: prefer fused attention for minibatches when estimated latency improvement >10%, otherwise prefer decode-optimized path. This cut regressions in staging.
2026-03-08: Operational decision: expose per-route bypass and compressor latency cap in Console; default to enabled for non-SLA routes.
2026-03-10: Canary approved (10% traffic) with automated metric alarms for p50/p95/p99 and KV-reuse ratio drops.
